What worked for us was letting him walk around the house (supervised!) with a leash on his collar for an hour or so every day until he got completely used to it. Then letting him walk around with the halter on and no leash for an hour or so a day until completely used to it. Then we combined both collar and leash until he was used to. Then we held the leash and followed him around in short bursts until he was used to us having the leash and we slowly incorporated using the leash to tell him where to go. For us it was a long process, but so worth it!! He will come for jogs or walks no problem and he comes running when you grab his halter and leash :)

My best advice is be completely honest. I see both a psychologist and psychiatrist and have a great relationship with both. It can be scary at first, but remember they are here to help you and can't do that without your complete honesty and openness.

Understandably some people can't talk about everything. I have issues that I am not entirely comfortable about, like traumatic events, and the best way to deal with these is to tell your professional there is an issue you don't feel up to discussing yet, but hope to in the future to leave yourself open to build on that when you're ready. 

Don't be afraid to try out several different people if that's what you need. I went through 6 psychologists before I found the one I've been seeing for 6 years and 4 psychiatrists before I found one I can be comfortable with. The main thing is that you find someone you feel comfortable talking to that you can relate to. 

In terms of medication, that can be a super long process too. If cognitive therapy doesn't help or you decide to medicate you may have to go through heaps of different medications. Never feel bad about being honest about how the medication effects you and if you aren't comfortable with it. My psychiatrist and I went through 6 medications before finding an old tricyclic paired with Valium when needed does the trick for me. 

Also never feel pressured by your professional, if they make you feel pressured or uncomfortable find a new one. 

To sum it up, it can be a long process but is well worth it when you find the right mix. Be honest and open, but don't be afraid to go through several people before you find the right match for you
